result:
A thousand words is a strange inheritance. It arrives without a will, without instructions, and I am expected to spend it all before the page runs out. If I were wise, I might invest in a single sharp idea and let it accrue meaning. If I were foolish, I might squander it on small talk with an invisible reader. But the truth is I am somewhere between, standing at the edge of a sentence, wondering whether the first word will be a door or a wall. The cursor blinks. It is patient. It simply waits here. It does not care.

I have always been suspicious of instructions that grant total freedom. Write whatever comes to you. It sounds generous, but it is also a dare. The blank page becomes a mirror, and suddenly I am not sure I want to look. What comes to me first is not an idea but a memory: being seven years old, sitting at a kitchen table, drawing a sun in the corner of a page because I did not know what else to put there. The sun had a face. It was smiling. I understood that filling space is easier with a familiar shape.

The problem with having exactly one thousand words is that each one begins to feel heavy. Some words are stones; some are feathers. I want to choose the ones that will leave a trace, but I cannot know in advance which they are. The word “trace” itself is good. It suggests a path already walked, a proof of presence. Maybe that is all writing is: leaving a trace across an otherwise silent surface, saying I was here, I thought this, I noticed. But the reader may not care. The reader may be skimming. And yet, here we are, together now.

I think about the people who write for a living, who must produce thousands of words a day, every day, whether they feel like it or not. Do they hoard words like coins, or do they learn to let them go easily, like breath? I imagine a novelist at a desk in the early morning, the window open, the sound of traffic beginning. She types a sentence, deletes it, types another. She does not have time to wait for inspiration. She has learned that inspiration is a shy animal that only appears when you are already working. I admire that.

Meaning. There it is. The big word. I have been avoiding it because it feels too large for this small task. But maybe meaning is not large. Maybe it is small and ordinary, like the particular blue of a mug, or the sound of rain on a metal roof, or the way a dog sighs before sleeping. We do not need to solve anything. We only need to pay attention. Attention is a form of love, someone said. I think that is true. If I pay attention, perhaps these words become love. That is enough. It is a small act.

But I also worry about beauty. It is easy to write beautifully about nothing. It is also easy to write plainly about everything. Which is better? I do not know. Some days I want sentences that glitter; other days I want sentences that disappear, leaving only the thing itself. Today I want both: a sentence that is a window and a sentence that is a hand reaching through the window. Perhaps that is greedy. But greed is just hunger that has forgotten its manners. And hunger is useful. It keeps us moving toward something real. That is enough for now.

Let me tell you something true. This morning I woke before the alarm and lay in the dark listening to the house settle. The walls creaked. The refrigerator hummed. Somewhere outside, a bird began to sing, very quietly, as if testing the day. I thought: this is the hour when the world is still unclaimed. No headlines, no emails, no voices. Just the slow machinery of being alive. I did not want to get up. But I did, because there was coffee to make, and because the day would not wait. That is not a metaphor. Or maybe it is.

I used to believe that writing was a way of escaping time. Now I think it is a way of entering time more fully. When I write, I am here, in this moment, with these words. The past is a story I tell; the future is a story I hope for. But the present is where the ink touches the page. It is the only place I can actually live. So this, right here, is a kind of practice. I am practicing being here. I am practicing being honest. I am practicing letting the words be what they are now.

There is a temptation to end with a grand conclusion, to tie everything together with a ribbon and call it wisdom. But life rarely offers ribbon. It offers thread, sometimes tangled, sometimes broken. Maybe the most honest ending is not a conclusion but a continuation. The words stop, but the thinking does not. The page ends, but the world does not. I can accept that. I can let the last word be ordinary. I can let it be a door left open. I can let it be a threshold. You may step through or not. The choice is yours now.

So here is what I will spend my final words on: a list of small things I love, because attention is love, and love is the only wealth that grows when you spend it. The smell of bread. The weight of a cat on my lap. The first sip of tea. A friend’s laugh. The color of the sky just after a storm. A sentence that surprises me. The quiet after rain. The sound of my own breathing. The knowledge that you have stayed with me this far. That is enough. That is more than enough. Thank you for reading.
